_comment: Enzyme activity registry. enzymes: genotype_activity is the clearance multiplier for that phenotype relative to a normal metaboliser, back-derived where possible from the AUC ratio of a sensitive substrate that is named in the note; phenotype_frequency is European. perpetrators: residual enzyme activity is NOT stored - it is derived at load time from index_auc_ratio and the index substrate's own index_fm, as residual = (1/ratio - (1 - fm)) / fm, and checked against the FDA class band. Reading a residual straight off the AUC ratio would overstate the remaining activity. CAVEAT: every index substrate here (desipramine, omeprazole, tizanidine, midazolam) was dosed ORALLY, so the ratios include gut-wall inhibition and loss of first-pass extraction and residuals derived from them overstate the purely hepatic effect - most for CYP3A4. A second caveat for genotype_activity: it is applied to one pathway, but several values were read off whole-drug exposure ratios without an fm correction; see each note. verified=true: the value was checked against the primary document named in source - an SPC or regulator label, the original study's full text (or its abstract, where the note says 'abstract only'), or a registry's posted results - and the note says where. verified=false: no primary could be reached, primaries disagree, or a field is calibrated rather than observed; the note says which. Drug-information aggregators and label mirrors are never a source for a verified value (tests/test_data_provenance.py).

CYP2D6.note: Not verifiable as a single number. Strattera label: atomoxetine AUC about 10-fold higher in poor metabolisers (1/10 = 0.10); its PK table, corrected for bioavailability (63 % vs 94 %), gives a clearance ratio of 0.128. Ultrarapid: the nortriptyline gene-copy series (Dalen 1998) implies about 1.33. Intermediate is the CPIC activity score 0.5, not a measured ratio. CAVEAT: the multiplier is applied to one pathway but derived from whole-drug ratios without an fm correction. Frequencies: phenotypic PM 7.0 % (Sachse 1997, 589 Germans); genotype-predicted European PM 5.44 % (Gaedigk 2017). Risperidone is deliberately not the anchor: its active moiety is CYP2D6-independent.

CYP2C19.note: Not verifiable as stated. Poor: oral omeprazole AUC ratios (7.5-fold, Klotz) are confounded by bioavailability; the IV arm of PMID 17203292 gives clearance multipliers of 0.23 (PM) and 0.58 (heterozygous EM). Ultrarapid 2.1 is exact (Baldwin 2008: *17/*17 omeprazole AUC 1973 vs 4151). The '12-fold' figure could not be traced. Poor-metaboliser frequency 0.03: Prilosec label, 'approximately 3% of Caucasians'. CPIC does not use activity scores for CYP2C19.

CYP2C9.note: Celebrex label: celecoxib systemic levels 3- to 7-fold higher in *3/*3 than in a pooled *1/*1 or *1/*3 group, so 0.14-0.33 and, against *1/*1 alone, lower. CPIC NSAID guideline: *3/*3 ratio of means 4.16. Intermediate 0.5 lumps *1/*2 (no effect) with *1/*3 (x1.62). No preset uses a CYP2C9 pathway.

CYP3A4.note: No poor/intermediate/ultrarapid system exists for CYP3A4, so there is no genotype selector - only inhibition and induction. 'normal' = 1.0 is the loader's normalisation, not a datum. The cited table is from a CYP3A4*22/tacrolimus meta-analysis and does not address phenotype classes. CYP3A5 expresser status is a separate axis not modelled here.

CYP1A2.note: No validated genotype-based activity multiplier; the *1F effect appears only alongside an inducer such as smoking (KNMP/DPWG background text, a guideline rather than a primary), so no genotype selector is offered.

perpetrators.name: Paroxetine 20 mg/day
perpetrators.note: Laine 2004 (abstract): paroxetine 20 mg/day for 8 days, single 100 mg desipramine, n=15, AUC x4.8. Index substrate desipramine, fm 0.85 = 1 - 15/102 from median clearances in poor vs extensive metabolisers (Brøsen 1993, abstract); this assumes no residual activity in poor metabolisers, whereas enzymes.json gives them 0.12, which would make fm about 0.97. Orally dosed, so the ratio includes first-pass loss.

perpetrators.name: Fluoxetine 20 mg/day
perpetrators.note: Preskorn 1994 (abstract): fluoxetine 20 mg/day, desipramine 50 mg/day at steady state, 18 healthy extensive metabolisers, AUC0-24 x4.8. The previously cited review table has no numbers. Index substrate desipramine, fm 0.85 = 1 - 15/102 from median clearances in poor vs extensive metabolisers (Brøsen 1993, abstract); this assumes no residual activity in poor metabolisers, whereas enzymes.json gives them 0.12, which would make fm about 0.97. Orally dosed, so the ratio includes first-pass loss.

perpetrators.name: Bupropion
perpetrators.note: Wellbutrin SR label: bupropion 150 mg b.i.d. with a single 50 mg desipramine, AUC 'approximately' 5-fold; the effect persists at least 7 days after the last dose. Index substrate desipramine, fm 0.85 = 1 - 15/102 from median clearances in poor vs extensive metabolisers (Brøsen 1993, abstract); this assumes no residual activity in poor metabolisers, whereas enzymes.json gives them 0.12, which would make fm about 0.97. Orally dosed, so the ratio includes first-pass loss.

perpetrators.name: Terbinafine
perpetrators.note: Lamisil label 7.1: desipramine AUC 5-fold (Madani 2002: 482 -> 2383 ng*h/mL, x4.94, terbinafine 250 mg/day for 21 days); still present at the last observation 4 weeks after stopping. Index substrate desipramine, fm 0.85 = 1 - 15/102 from median clearances in poor vs extensive metabolisers (Brøsen 1993, abstract); this assumes no residual activity in poor metabolisers, whereas enzymes.json gives them 0.12, which would make fm about 0.97. Orally dosed, so the ratio includes first-pass loss.

perpetrators.name: Fluvoxamine 50 mg/day
perpetrators.note: Yasui-Furukori 2004 (Br J Clin Pharmacol 57:487) Table 1: fluvoxamine 25 mg b.i.d. (50 mg/day, not 100-150) for 6 days, single 40 mg omeprazole, homozygous extensive metabolisers, AUC ratio of geometric means 8340/1483 = 5.62 (the text's 6.2-fold is a mean of individual ratios). Inhibition is dose-dependent. Index substrate omeprazole: fm 0.85 is not established by any primary; the primaries bracket it at 0.84-0.90 (1 - 1/6.29 = 0.84 from Kang 2002; 0.87-0.90 from Yasui-Furukori's poor vs homozygous extensive metabolisers). Orally dosed, so the ratio includes first-pass loss.

perpetrators.name: Fluconazole
perpetrators.note: Kang 2002 (abstract): fluconazole 100 mg/day for 4 days, omeprazole 20 mg, n=18 healthy men, AUC0-inf 491 -> 3090 ng*h/mL (x6.29). Diflucan label: strong CYP2C19, moderate CYP2C9 and CYP3A4 inhibitor; this entry covers CYP2C19 only. Index substrate omeprazole: fm 0.85 is not established by any primary; the primaries bracket it at 0.84-0.90 (1 - 1/6.29 = 0.84 from Kang 2002; 0.87-0.90 from Yasui-Furukori's poor vs homozygous extensive metabolisers). Orally dosed, so the ratio includes first-pass loss.

perpetrators.name: Ciprofloxacin
perpetrators.note: Index substrate: Lower bound from the 33-fold AUC rise with fluvoxamine (range 14-103x).

perpetrators.name: Fluvoxamine
perpetrators.note: Range 14-103x. Index substrate: Lower bound from the 33-fold AUC rise with fluvoxamine (range 14-103x).

perpetrators.name: Ketoconazole 200 mg b.i.d.
perpetrators.note: Index substrate: Published static-model value. ORAL ratios also carry gut-wall CYP3A4 (ketoconazole raises oral midazolam 11-20x but intravenous only 2.7-4.7x), so a residual derived from an oral ratio OVERSTATES the hepatic effect on drugs whose fm is hepatic.
